conviction_note: The one genuinely off-consensus item I found — an IEEPA tariff refund Macy's explicitly excluded from guidance — is near-certain to inflate headline EPS, but the two department stores with the identical 13-week quarter already ran this exact experiment in August and their stocks paid nothing for it (DDS -3.5%, KSS -0.06%); with 25d skew at -15.7 (calls bid) the upside case is the side already being paid for, so I take a small negative rather than the large positive the beat superficially implies.

findings.finding: Macy's told the Street on 2026-06-04 that IEEPA tariff refunds are 'not incorporated in our outlook', yet both department stores with the identical quarter-end (1 Aug 2026) booked large refunds in that quarter — Kohl's ~$150m received, ~$100m through gross margin; Dillard's $37.2m, $1.82/share — and both stocks fell or went nowhere on the resulting monster beats, so the near-certain headline beat at Macy's is worth roughly nothing and possibly less than nothing to the price.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q2 consensus of $0.37 embeds a 9.8% YoY EPS *decline* and the Zacks metric detail published 2026-09-04 carries no refund line at all; the investing.com preview published this morning (2026-09-09) contains zero mentions of tariff refunds, Kohl's or Dillard's. If the read-across were priced, consensus would not still be modelling a YoY decline and the FY Street number would not sit at $2.23 against a company guide of $2.00-$2.20. The unpriced part is not the beat — it is the reaction function: at -15.7 vol points of skew the option market is paying up for calls into a catalyst whose two nearest analogues, three and four weeks ago, produced -3.5% and -0.1% because both were punished on the top line while the one-time gain was discounted entirely. Second-order risk in the same cluster and pointing the same way: the CIT's July order gives a confirmed refund path only to importers that sued, Macy's is not identifiable among the CIT plaintiffs and its own language was that 'timing and amounts remain uncertain' — so Macy's may book materially less than the ~$0.24 Jefferies has publicly penciled in, or nothing, while peers banked theirs.
findings.independence: Dillard's 8-K/release of 2026-08-13 quantifies the same catalyst independently at $37.2m ($1.82/share) with the stock closing down ~3.5% that day: https://investor.dillards.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dillards-inc-reports-second-quarter-and-year-date-results-3 . Separately, Holland & Knight (2026-07-27) documents that non-plaintiff importers have no confirmed refund path: https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/07/file-now-cits-order-confirms-only-importers-that-have-sued . These are different documents from the Kohl's 8-K but sit in one tariff-refund source cluster with it — treat as one finding, not three.

findings.finding: Sell-side models Q2 credit card revenue at $166.2m, +8.6% YoY, but management guided on 2026-06-04 that credit card growth would decelerate to 'more in line with the overall business' — roughly +1% to +2% on a $153m base, i.e. about $156m — a ~$10m gap on a line that drops straight to EBIT in a quarter consensus puts at only ~$0.37 of EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus line item is published (Zacks, 2026-09-04) at +8.6% while the company's own stated forward growth rate is low single digit; if the market had reconciled the two, the modelled 'other revenue' of $200.2m would have been marked down toward the FY $920m other-revenue guide's implied run-rate rather than extrapolating Q1's +11.7%. Nobody writes previews off a guidance verb ('more in line with the overall business') because it carries no number, which is exactly why it survives unmodelled.
findings.independence: Consensus segment detail from a different source, Zacks via Yahoo 2026-09-04: https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/wall-streets-insights-key-metrics-131503279.html . No third source corroborates the deceleration; Citi's own card master-trust delinquency and charge-off data (July 2026: delinquencies 1.32%, NCO 1.90%) shows portfolio credit still benign, which cuts the other way and is why the band is wide and the size small.

searched_and_found_nothing: Citi credit-card master-trust monthly delinquency/charge-off series as a lead on the Macy's profit share — the trust that files publicly is Citi's own branded-card Issuance Trust, not the Citi Retail Services private-label book that houses Macy's, and the published July 2026 data (delinquencies 1.32%, NCO 1.90%) shows nothing deteriorating; the door named as the best one in the brief is not actually mapped to this line
Renewed Arkhouse/Brigade takeover activity — everything found dates to 2024 and mid-2025, nothing in 2026, so the -15.7 calls-bid skew is not explained by a live bid
Macy's 8-K filings since 2026-06-03 — there are none; no pre-announcement, no material event, no quiet 8-K
Insider Form 4 clusters — only routine director RSU/phantom grants and one SVP/controller sale of 10,077 shares at $25.63 on 2026-06-25; no buying cluster

Macy's as a named plaintiff in the CIT IEEPA refund litigation — could not confirm either way from public search, which is itself the reason the refund size is uncertain rather than a finding on its own
Real-estate/asset-sale gains as a swing factor — Q1 2026 was $15m against Q2 2025's $16m and Q2 2024's $36m, no evidence of a lumpy Q2 2026 monetisation
A company-specific cause for the -8.1% 20-day drawdown — general-merchandise retail is down ~5.6% over the same month, so most of it is sector beta, not a Macy's signal
Census department-store-specific sales for May-July 2026 — only the headline retail aggregate was retrievable (June +0.2% m/m, July -0.6% m/m), no department-store line
baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline's clearest directional statement — the 25-delta skew of -15.7 says the market is paying up for calls into this print, and my read of the two nearest peer precedents says the beat those calls are being bought for is the part the market has already learned to discount; it also cuts against the pipeline's best free control, since a -8.1% run-up would argue for a bounce, which is why the size is small and the band is wide.
